title: 2025 budget service expansions and transit staffing
subtitle: Housing, homelessness, climate and library hours, service reduction options, police budget motion deferred, and capital deferral options.
overview: The Strategic Planning and Budget Committee went through deferred 2025 service expansions one by one. It recommended sending most transit requests to final budget day on December 11, at reduced staffing levels. Transit core network staffing was cut to 8 FTEs, operational adjustments to 5 FTEs and support staff to 13 FTEs. A mid-year start was set for one traffic analyst.

The committee also recommended carrying forward part-time library hours, an accessibility advisor, two housing support positions, the plan to end chronic homelessness, bylaw officers for encampments and a legal assistant. It rejected several roles, including a tenant access coordinator, a transportation communications specialist, a climate program manager (tied vote) and several finance and IT positions. Nothing is final until Council decides.

After a closed session, the committee directed staff to publish service reduction options by 4:30 p.m. on November 29 and to hold a public input meeting on December 3. Revenue-offset expansions were also moved to final budget day. A motion asking the police board to cut $4 million was deferred to December 3. Staff reported the removals lowered the projected levy impact by about 0.44 percentage points of tax impact.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended adding 8 transit core network FTEs to the 2025 budget, half the 16 requested, {{vote:m1}}, with the final vote on the amended item {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended 5 FTEs for customer-driven operational adjustments instead of 9, {{vote:m4}}.
The committee recommended 13 FTEs for transit service support, down from the 24 first requested, {{vote:m7}}.
The committee recommended one traffic systems management analyst instead of three, {{vote:m9}}.
The committee did not recommend the climate and sustainability program manager, which was defeated on a tied vote {{vote:m14}}, even after the start date was moved to June 1, 2025.
The committee recommended 2 FTEs for housing tenancy supports {{vote:m18}}, but rejected the third, a tenant access coordinator {{vote:m19}}.
The committee recommended sending the plan's implementation investments to final budget day {{vote:m20}}, with staff to report on possible funding from another level of government.

decisions.item: Service reduction options and public input
decisions.detail: The committee directed staff to include and publish service reduction options by November 29 and schedule a public input meeting for December 3 {{vote:m31}}.

debate: Some councillors objected that the deferred expansions were bundled into one motion when they expected line-by-line review. Others said they wanted a fuller view of the budget, such as debenture options, before cutting positions. The committee agreed to vote on each item individually.

On transit, staff said core network FTEs respond to crowding and bus pass-ups, and that the 16 originally requested depended on a service plan not yet presented. One councillor argued one year of crowding was a sacrifice taxpayers could bear, while others said transit is a necessity for vulnerable residents. Staff said support-staff cuts would mean more overtime, though unsafe buses would not run.

On the communications specialist and climate manager, some councillors called the roles useful but not essential in a tight year. Staff said the communications role would free engineers for technical work. They said the climate role would support home retrofit and community adaptation work beyond the grant-funded pilot.

On housing, staff said the new positions support about 150 new units and that mixed-income rents could raise revenue, and they offered to confirm the figures before December 11. One councillor questioned whether the tenant access coordinator would effectively give legal advice. Staff said the role refers tenants to legal clinics.

On the police budget motion, some councillors supported asking the police board to look again. Others objected to the wording, said the board had already reviewed the budget, or noted many members were absent, and the motion was deferred.
